text:
maria.p: Heads-up — APAC firewall is moving from fw-lite to default-deny on 2025-03-26 02:00 UTC. This will block the endpoint our node-provisioner uses to fetch session keys. I think new GPU nodes will fail to finish bootstrap unless we allow the provisioning path.
raj: Ugh. Which exact call is getting blocked?
theo: It's the vault-proxy /session-grant call — `POST https://vault-proxy.apac.internal/v1/session/grant` returns 403 during canary.
ops-bot: [deploy] fw-rollout scheduled: apac-firewall-default-deny v2 -> 02:00 UTC. Noted by @maria.p.
maria.p: Per initial tests, the error is `access denied: iam condition mismatch`. The provisioning role needs `kms:GenerateDataKey` + `kms:Decrypt` to unwrap node bootstrap secrets.
lina: If we open those permissions broadly we lose audit guarantees. Security prefers a narrow allowlist.
security-bot: ALERT: any grant for kms:GenerateDataKey must trigger audit-relay for 48h retention. Policy: `audit-relay:on-grant` tag required.
raj: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) temporary allowlist for `vault-proxy` IPs in fw rules for the 3-hour provision window; 2) issue short-lived delegations to the provisioning SA with a forced audit-relay tag.
theo: Option 1 is fastest. Ops can flip an allowlist rule at 01:50 UTC, revert at 05:00 UTC. But warm-pool churn could keep nodes trying past the window.
maria.p: Cost note: if onboarding stalls, warm pool keeps spinning GPUs idle — rough calc from last time: ~120 GPU-hours => ~$2.8k/day. Need to avoid repeated failed boot loops.
lina: Option 2 (short-lived delegations) is better for compliance, but needs tooling changes to attach the `audit:relay=true` label and persist to cloudtrail. Who owns that flow?
raj: That's us (platform) + security. We can script a grant flow with TTL=15m and auto-revoke. Patchpoint: `./scripts/grant-provisioner.sh --ttl 15m --tag audit-relay`
(theo posts): ```bash
# quick grant hack (needs security sign-off)
aws iam create-policy-version --policy-arn arn:aws:iam::redwood:policy/ProvisionerTemp \
  --policy-document file://provisioner-temp.json --set-as-default
./scripts/attach-temp.sh provisioner-role --ttl 900 --tag audit-relay:true
```
security-bot: REMINDER: Temporary policies must be recorded in the policy-change log and an incident ticket created: #sec-audit-bridge.
maria.p: Proposed plan: ops applies allowlist for vault-proxy IPs for 4h as immediate unblock. Simultaneously platform + security land the short-lived delegation automation by EOD. After delegation flow tested, revert allowlist.
lina: Approve the plan with one constraint: every delegation run must include the `audit-relay` header and push to SIEM within 5 minutes.
raj: I'll own the allowlist flip and the rollback cron. Will post the script and IPs in this thread 30m before.
theo: I'll prototype the delegation script and send a PR against infra-scripts. Need someone from security for a quick review.
maria.p: Thanks — ping @lina for review once PR is up. Also adding monitoring: create alert if >5 failed bootstrap attempts in 10m (to catch partial rollouts).
ops-bot: [alert rule created] gpu-bootstrap-fail-rate (threshold=5/10m) by raj.
security-bot: Note: any change to firewall rules requires an RFC in #infra-rfcs and a short_change tag. Please file before 01:00 UTC.
raj: Filing RFC now. Will link here.
maria.p: TL;DR: Immediate short allowlist window to prevent GPU onboarding waste, concurrent work to add short-lived, auditable delegations. Followups: RFC link, PR link, allowlist script.
